Physics hand-checked: the book's answer ('IT IS AMAMMOTH ENCYCLOPEDIA OF KNOWLEDGE', a run-on of 'a mammoth') is reworded here in plain literal English with the same content — a very large store of information on internet-connected computers, open to everyone at any time.

recall_prompt: Say what the World Wide Web is — what it holds, where that is stored, and who can reach it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What the Web is
steps.mark_note: A large information store on the internet
lines: The World Wide Web is a very large store
of information kept on computers that are
steps.margin_note: First mark. Information, stored on computers connected to the internet.
steps.why: The definition has two parts that both matter: WHAT the Web holds (information) and WHERE that lives (on computers connected to the internet). Leaving either out makes the answer a slogan.
common_mistakes: Writing that the Web and the internet are the same thing. The internet is the network of computers; the Web is the information stored and shared on it.
Calling it a device or a machine. It is a store of information, not hardware.

recall.must_convey: That the World Wide Web is a very large store of information held on computers connected to the internet.
accept: a very large store of information
an encyclopedia of knowledge on the internet
reject: anyone can read it at any time

steps.memory_tip: Two parts: what it holds (information) and where it lives (computers on the internet).

steps.label: Who can reach it, and how
steps.mark_note: Open to everyone at any time
lines: Anyone can read it at any time of day,
through a computer connected to the

lines.text: WWW: information for everyone, any time

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Everyone, at any time, through an internet-connected computer.
steps.why: What makes the Web useful is open access: it is not limited to one place, one time or one group. The book states this too, in its 'accessible to every one round the clock' line.
common_mistakes: Leaving out how it is reached. Access is through a computer connected to the internet.
Saying only some people can use it. The Web is open to everyone with an internet connection.

recall.must_convey: That anyone can reach the Web at any time through a computer connected to the internet.
accept: open to everyone at any time
reached through a computer connected to the internet
anyone with an internet connection can use it
reject: a very large store of information

steps.memory_tip: Three alls: all people, all hours, all through the internet.

insider_note: First mark: information stored on internet-connected computers. Second mark: open to everyone at any time. The book's own wording is a run-on in capitals — write it plainly.
